title: Fabric data agent API is now public: Build Fabric data agents into your tools and pipelines
summary: A Fabric Updates Blog post announcing general availability of a public management-plane API for Fabric data agents, letting the existing data agent SDK run outside a Fabric notebook — from a developer's own machine, CI/CD pipeline, container, or backend service — for creating, configuring, updating, and publishing agents programmatically.
audience: Developers and platform teams automating data agent provisioning across many workspaces, ISVs embedding data agents into their own products, and DevOps engineers wiring agent lifecycle management into CI/CD.
why_it_matters: This turns the data agent SDK from an in-notebook, one-workspace-at-a-time tool into a scriptable management-plane surface, which is the mechanism that lets architects standardize and promote agent configuration the same way they already do for other Fabric items via Git and deployment pipelines.
takeaways: The headline change is where the SDK can run: previously notebook-only inside Fabric, now also outside Fabric on the standard Fabric public REST API surface with the same auth patterns as other Fabric automation.

This is explicitly a management-plane API for lifecycle operations (create/configure/update/publish), not the runtime query path; the MCP endpoint remains the consumption surface once an agent is published.

The API is positioned as complementary to, not a replacement for, Fabric Git integration and deployment pipelines, which already track agent configuration as files and promote it across environments at the workspace level.
A minimal script pattern is shown: authenticate, create an agent, attach a data source with instructions, then publish a staged draft.

The target scenarios are explicitly automation-at-scale: repeating one agent shape across many workspaces, building an internal portal, CI/CD-driven provisioning, and ISVs shipping data agents as part of their own product.

claims.text: The Fabric data agent SDK, previously usable only from inside a Fabric notebook, now also runs on the general Fabric public REST API, so it can execute from a developer's local machine, CI/CD pipeline, container, or backend service outside Fabric.

Through the newly public API, code can programmatically create and manage data agent artifacts, add and configure data sources, set agent and data-source instructions and example queries, and update or publish agents, without going through the Fabric portal UI.

The data agent public API and SDK are explicitly a management-plane surface for lifecycle operations (creating, configuring, updating, publishing); after a data agent is published, the MCP endpoint remains the separate runtime surface used to query it from tools, applications, or agent experiences.

The data agent public API uses the same authentication and request patterns as the rest of the Fabric public API that already covers workspaces and items, so it integrates into existing Fabric automation without a separate auth model.

The public API is designed to complement, not replace, Fabric Git integration and deployment pipelines: Git and deployment pipelines track and promote agent configuration as files at the workspace level, while the public API adds a programmatic layer for creating, updating, and publishing agents directly from code.

A minimal outside-Fabric workflow authenticates with an Azure credential (for example AzureCliCredential), creates a data agent scoped to a target workspace ID via create_data_agent, attaches a data source and agent instructions via update_settings and add_staging_datasource, then calls publish_staging to publish it.

The intended use cases named for the public API are provisioning the same data agent shape repeatably across many workspaces, building internal tools/portals that manage agents without opening Fabric, wiring agent provisioning into existing CI/CD pipelines, and ISVs embedding data agents as part of their own product rather than a side experience in Fabric.

Reference documentation for the newly public surface is split into a Data Agent Items API for managing agent lifecycle and a separate Staging API for editing data sources and example queries before publish.
